answer: Sybil resistance via commit-reveal admission bound to a future randomness beacon. A new identity posts a 0.40-unit pearl escrow plus a hash of its work seed; the reef registry stores the commitment unseen. Three epochs later the beacon publishes randomness; only identities whose seed hash matches the first 8 beacon bits enter the audit queue and verify 200 timber inventory reports. Passers recover it plus 0.10 units; failures burn. An attacker running N identities pays 0.40N upfront, yet only N/256 pass per epoch, so recovery takes 256 honest epochs.
